newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico beer exports hit record $52.8 mln in April.
newsitem.headline: Mexico beer exports hit record $52.8 mln in April.

text.p: Mexican beer exports reached $52.8 million in April, the highest monthly total among records dating to 1980, the national statistics institute INEGI said on Monday.
The April total, which was 66.6 percent higher than the same month a year ago, surpassed the previous record of $42.6 million set in July 1996, INEGI said.

In the first four months of the year, the two exporting beer companies, Grupo Modelo and FEMSA, posted export sales of $149.9 million, up 31.6 percent compared to the first four months of 1996, INEGI said.
One Mexico City-based beverage analyst said the increase likely can be attributed more to Modelo than FEMSA.

"The exports from Grupo Modelo in the second quarter were higher than what they expected," Marco Vera of Deutche Morgan Grenfell told Reuters. "They were expected an 18 percent increase (in sales volume) for the whole year but now it probably will be higher."
The company will announce official sales volumes figures in July along with the rest of its second-quarter results.
An official at Grupo Modelo told Reuters on Monday that export volumes are expected to rise from 18 to 20 percent this year, but probably "closer to 20 percent."
Grupo Modelo exported 3.72 million hectoliters of beer in 1996, up 28.7 percent over 1995.
In the first quarter, Modelo exported 1.02 million hectoliters, up 23 percent over the Q1 sales in 1996.
Modelo's export growth has been led by Pacifo, one of five export brands, which posted Q1 sales 94 percent higher in 1997 over Q1 1996.
((--Tomas de la Rosa, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-7912))
